title: Tooltips and explainers
note: Written for this portal in plain English. Each screen has a short explainer and, where it helps, a line for the person reading it. Choose who you are in the explainer bar; nothing is sent anywhere and the choice stays on this device.

personas.label: Everyone
personas.lens: Hover over or focus on any drawer item or underlined term to see what it means.

personas.label: Young person, 11 to 15
personas.lens: You can use most of Amplify on your own. Ask a parent, carer or teacher before joining an outside group or sharing anything with your name on it.

personas.label: Young person, 16 to 25
personas.lens: You can take part directly: campaign, volunteer, contribute to this portal and become an ambassador.

personas.label: Parent, guardian or carer
personas.lens: You can support a young person to take part, act on their behalf where a service is age-limited, and keep them safe while they speak up.

personas.label: Youth worker or group leader
personas.lens: Use these screens to plan sessions, run campaigns with your group, and follow safeguarding rules for any outside activity.

personas.label: Teacher, tutor or school staff
personas.lens: Most screens map to citizenship, PSHE, computing and careers lessons, and to UK Parliament Week activities.

personas.label: Coding or STEM club leader or mentor
personas.lens: The Get involved and STEM screens turn this portal into a real open-source project your club can learn from and contribute to.

personas.label: Councillor, policy maker, researcher or journalist
personas.lens: Every fact links to its source and date; the Media centre has approved descriptions and the rules for using them.

home.tip: Start here: what Amplify is, who it is for, and quick routes in.

for.young11: Try the New here tour first.
for.parent: Try the Parents and carers tour.

corner.tip: The values behind youth voice: participation, equality, education and empowerment.

route.tip: A step-by-step route into youth voice that fits your age, where you live and how much time you have.

for.young11: Pick your nation and age to see what you can join now.

state.tip: How the UK is governed: Parliament, the devolved governments, councils, and where young people can be heard.

for.teacher: Works as a citizenship lesson starter.

issues.tip: The issues young people raise most, from votes at 16 to transport and mental health.

guide.tip: Guided tours and how to use each part of the portal.

hub.tip: Campaign hub: the petition story, real figures and what happened next.

momentum.tip: A planning model for how fast a relaunched campaign would need to grow. It is a calculation, not a forecast.

plan.tip: Pick a launch window around exams and holidays and check you are ready.

coal.tip: Who could back a campaign: organisations, networks and allies.

kit.tip: Templates and messages to adapt for your campaign. Check generated text before you use it.

pledge.tip: Shows how a pledge wall would work. The pledges are sample text, not real people.

radar.tip: News and moments worth acting on, with dates.

policy.tip: The policies and strategies that affect young people across the UK nations.

for.ally: Each entry links to the official document.

map.tip: Find constituencies and local routes on a map.

acad.tip: Short lessons on democracy, campaigning and speaking up.

for.teacher: Each lesson can be run in about 20 minutes.

ysc.tip: The Youth Select Committee: how it works and what it has looked at.

post.tip: What past campaigns learned, so the next one goes further.

track.tip: What has actually changed because young people spoke up.

prof.tip: Members of Youth Parliament and the regions and nations they represent.

incl.tip: Reaching every young person, including those least often heard.

res.tip: Resources sorted by setting: school, youth club, home, online.

ai.tip: How AI tools and app connectors could help, and their limits. Concept only.

brand.tip: The portal's shapes, colours and type, and how to use them.

care.tip: Safeguarding and support: who to contact if you are worried, now or later.

for.young11: If you are in danger now, call 999.
for.parent: Helplines here are checked every 30 days.

graph.tip: A glossary of terms and how the ideas in this portal connect.

sources.tip: Trusted sources for young people, filterable by theme, nation and audience, each with its check date.

latest.tip: What's new for young people in the UK, dated and sourced.

changes.tip: The release log: what changed in the portal and when.

trust.tip: Safeguards by audience, age and access rules, sign languages and every voice.

health.tip: The portal's own health checks, freshness and open issues, in public.

about.tip: Who is behind Amplify, why it exists and what it aims to achieve.

launch.tip: The UK Parliament Week launch plan, with calendar and sharing links.

communities.tip: Youth parliaments, councils, clubs and networks where young people already meet.

media.tip: Approved descriptions, key facts with sources, and illustrations you can use.

help.tip: The user manual, adoption guide, tutorials and answers to common questions.

feedback.tip: Suggest an idea, report a bug or get in touch, all through forms.

involve.tip: Ways to help build, check and look after this portal, matched to your time and skills.

for.young11: Under 13s can help through a trusted adult; 13 and over can use GitHub with a parent's or carer's agreement.
for.club: A ready-made open-source project for your club, with real checks and real reviews.

ambassadors.tip: Become a supporter, champion or ambassador: what each role does and how to start.

for.worker: Ambassadors under 18 need a named adult contact.

campaign.tip: Posters, social posts, an assembly script and a calendar of moments to spread the word.

for.young11: Social media posts are for adults or allies to share on a young person's behalf.

learn.tip: Training sessions you can run: plans, timings, outcomes and materials.

for.teacher: Sessions map to citizenship, PSHE, computing and careers.

stem.tip: A shout-out for young people in STEM, especially girls and young women in coding, engineering, architecture and DevOps.

for.young11: Coding clubs are free and you do not need to know anything to start.
for.club: Includes a DevOps learning path built on this portal's own pipeline.

research.tip: Take part in user research, or help with UI, UX, graphic and content design, safely and without giving your name in public.

for.young11: Under 16s take part with a parent's or carer's consent, and never alone with a researcher.
for.worker: Your group can take part together, in your setting and under your safeguarding policy.
for.teacher: Content testing and card sorting work well as a lesson activity.

myp.tip: Member of Youth Parliament: a young person aged 11 to 18, elected to represent their area in the UK Youth Parliament.

makeyourmark.tip: The UK's largest youth ballot, which chooses the issues the UK Youth Parliament debates.

votes16.tip: Lowering the voting age to 16 for UK general elections. 16 and 17 year olds can already vote in Scottish and Welsh parliament and council elections.

selectcommittee.tip: A group of MPs or peers who look into a subject and report. The Youth Select Committee is the young people's version.

safeguarding.tip: Protecting children and young people from harm, and acting when you are worried about someone.

dbs.tip: A criminal record check for adults working with young people: DBS in England and Wales, PVG in Scotland and AccessNI in Northern Ireland.

agecheck.tip: Ways online services check a user's age, required for some content under the Online Safety Act.

provenance.tip: Where a fact came from. V means verified against the source, S means found by search, and K means a lead still to confirm.

moscow.tip: A way to prioritise: Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have this time.

opensource.tip: Code anyone can read, learn from and suggest changes to. This portal's code is open on GitHub.

issue.tip: A note on GitHub describing an idea, a bug or a question. Anyone 13 or over with an account can open one.

pullrequest.tip: A proposed change to the code or content. A person reviews it, and automated checks must pass, before it is accepted.

ci.tip: Automated checks that run on every proposed change, so mistakes are caught before they reach the portal.

devops.tip: Building, testing, releasing and running software together, with automation, so changes are small, safe and frequent.

wcag.tip: The international accessibility standard this portal aims to meet, so disabled people can use it.

bsl.tip: British Sign Language and Irish Sign Language, both recognised in law in the UK.

ukpw.tip: An annual week of events about democracy for young people across the UK. Amplify launches during it in November 2026.

rc.tip: A version that is ready to test but not yet launched.

ui.portal: Show the portal: the full set of screens with the drawer on the left.
ui.both: Show the portal and the app concept side by side.
ui.app: Show the app view, a design concept for a future phone app. It is not a real app yet.
ui.access: Access and language settings: text size, contrast, motion, dyslexia-friendly type and languages.
ui.persona: Choose who you are to tailor the explainers. The choice stays on this device and is never sent anywhere.
